candidates.text: The ticket came in a pale envelope with a postmark from the town I left at nineteen, and the stub inside was the colour of weak tea — thirty years of damp in the paper — except that the date on it was tomorrow's, roller-printed in the same dot-matrix drum the machine had used back then, the 7 with its crossbar sitting slightly off, as though the machine had been dragged out of a cupboard and warmed up for the occasion. It was a return. The outward half had been punched — a small round hole with a little starburst of ink around it — and the return half was virgin, still carrying its fare of £2.40 in the old money, and I understood, sitting on the kitchen floor with the kettle going cold beside me, that I had never used it: I had missed the connection, or lost my nerve, or simply been too young to want to go back. So the return had stayed valid in the only way a paper can stay valid — by never being tested. Then I looked up the route, because the ticket said 47A, and the 47A had been withdrawn the following winter when the bypass opened, and it had not run since. Except it was running tomorrow. One service, one day, the last ever, the company had announced, and every unused return from the old stock was being posted out, automatically, to whoever the envelopes had names on. By Thursday there were forty of us at the stop with our tickets, all different years, all the same yellow, and the conductor was a girl with the ancient machine slung in a canvas bag, and she punched each one without comment, and none of us got on, because the bus was going out to the depot first, and then out again along the coast road, and if we wanted, we could go as far as it went. I have never been so glad to have missed a bus in my life.

instruction: Answer the brief, but make it creative.

task.brief: A bus ticket bought thirty years ago arrives in the post, dated tomorrow. Write the next paragraph.
good_idea_qualities: the ticket forces a small concrete decision
the paragraph makes the elapsed thirty years felt without explaining them
the ending leaves the reader uneasy rather than resolved
task.reference_text: The envelope had been forwarded twice and the postmark was this morning's. Inside, the ticket was warm, as though it had been held, and the destination printed on it was the town she had left at nineteen without telling anyone she was going.
